title: Screenshot harmonization pipeline: automated redaction, aspect-safe cropping, and locale-aware variants
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and define a repeatable pipeline to produce brand-consistent UI screenshots and quickstart assets that are safe for public docs and localized across regions. The pipeline must: 1) detect and remove or mask PII and customer-specific strings (API keys, emails, account IDs), 2) crop and export images with aspect-safe framing for different product contexts (docs hero, in-app tour, mobile quickstart), and 3) generate locale-aware variants (date formats, currency labels, language overlays) without introducing visual inconsistency. Focus is on predictable, automatable outputs that reduce manual designer time while preserving accessibility and brand tone.

Define content-detection spec: regex rules + ML model outputs used by engineering - owner: Asha Patel
Create cropping heuristics doc: center-of-interest rules per screen type + fallback safe-areas - owner: Riley Chen
Design locale overlay patterns for date/currency/units and language-specific truncation rules - owner: Sofia Martinez
Produce example asset pack (3 screens x 3 sizes x 4 locales) for engineering integration tests - owner: Riley Chen
Accessibility review: contrast and alt-text guidance for generated screenshots - owner: Jordan Lee
Ship rollout plan: canary docs inclusion and manual QA gate - owner: Asha Patel
acceptance_criteria: Automated pipeline produces PNG/SVG assets matching brand tokens and screenshot size matrix (hero, doc-inline, mobile) without visible PII
Localization variants render localized strings/units and maintain layout without overlap or truncation in 95% of sample pages
Redaction preserves layout and spacing so that downstream screenshot cropping does not break composition
Design tokens and Figma components published to design system library and linked in Confluence
Engineering integration tests pass with sample asset pack and metadata tags (locale, screen-type, template-id)
deliverables: Figma library: Redaction overlay components + crop guides
Technical spec: detection rules + file naming and metadata schema (Confluence link)
Asset pack: canonical inputs and expected outputs (PNG 1x/2x, webp)
QA checklist: visual checks, automated diff rules, and accessibility checks
Rollout doc: canary plan, owner list, and rollback criteria
comments: 2026-03-02 - Asha Patel: Kickoff: scoped for docs and quickstart flows only. Not handling user-generated images in product at this stage.

2026-03-04 - Riley Chen: Early mockups uploaded to Figma. Shared three redaction styles (solid fill, patterned mask, blurred). Preference from design review leans toward solid brand-color mask with optional hashed placeholder for traceability.

2026-03-05 - Miguel Ortega (Eng): Engineering note - detection will be hybrid: regex for common tokens + lightweight OCR for free text. Need clear metadata contract for 'masked_regions' to avoid layout shifts when cropping.

2026-03-06 - Jordan Lee: Accessibility review - avoid pure black masks; ensure 4.5:1 contrast against surrounding backgrounds when used inline. Provide alt-text templates when screenshots are auto-generated.
2026-03-09 - Sofia Martinez: Localization edge case: right-to-left (RTL) screens require mirrored cropping anchors; adding a rule to flip padding anchors for RTL locales.

2026-03-11 - Asha Patel: Decision log: choose solid matte mask in brand charcoal with 12% corner radius for rounded UI elements. Blur is not acceptable due to OCR leakage and inconsistent results across devices.
2026-03-12 - Riley Chen: Uploaded asset pack to drive and opened initial PR for export script. Requesting engineering review on naming conventions and metadata fields. See links below.
